what: Named, hand-verified filings for the Roth / voluntary-after-tax flags. Pinned BY ACK, with the ROLE each one plays, so an instrument that stops reproducing its own motivating case fails loudly instead of printing a smaller number. A count that omits its own motivating case looks exactly like a count that includes it. 2026-11-22: ten cases, nine added for v208. The two the brief named for WITHDRAWAL (Asphalt Materials, Arcadium Lithium) are pinned must-KEEP instead, because reading their filings says so and because the accuracy-log entry they came from lists them among a terminal veto's genuine ERRORS rather than among its targets.

roles.denial: the published quote's own words DENY the flag it is published under — defect 1, docs/accuracy-log.md 2026-11-20
roles.subsequent-future: the flag is caused, or would be re-caused after a repair upstream, by an affirmative sentence inside a subsequent-events / plan-amendment section whose effective date falls AFTER the reported plan year — defect 2
roles.must-keep: a correct published yes, verified by reading the filing. A veto that withdraws this one is too wide and must not ship.
roles.must-stay-withdrawn: v207 WITHDREW this flag and the withdrawal was right. The ack is therefore CORRECTLY ABSENT from the published-yes population, and a tool that treats that absence as a missing pin is reporting its own bookkeeping as a defect — subsequent-events-size.mjs exited 1 on exactly that the first time it ran after the v207 merge. The claim is now the other way round and it is STRONGER than the one it replaces: if this ack ever publishes this arm again, a later change has undone v207 and the pin must FAIL. Nothing else in the repo guards the shipped fix against regression.
roles.must-withdraw: the candidate under test EXISTS to withdraw this published yes, and the member was READ in its own filing. Unlike `subsequent-future`, which merely describes a known-wrong yes and NOTES when a candidate leaves it alone, this FAILS the gate when the flag survives: a ship whose claim is a withdrawal must make it. Added 2026-11-22 for v208 (the date test in the roth and after-tax arms). It inherits the UNTESTED handling, so a plan whose stored flag the baseline cannot reproduce from local text is reported and never failed.

cases.verified: 2026-11-20, filing read: "After-tax contributions are not permitted by the Plan." and ZERO occurrences of Roth anywhere. The store holds afterTax: true and app.js:4080 renders it as "✓ Available". WITHDRAWN BY v207 (2026-11-21): the store now holds the flag FALSE with the denial quote retained as the evidence for the withdrawal, mirrored 13a445fb. The pin's role flips to must-stay-withdrawn: this arm reappearing means a later change undid v207.
cases.quote: After-tax contributions are not permitted by the 6 Plan.

cases.verified: 2026-11-20, filing read: the contributions note says "The Plan does not allow for Roth or after-tax contributions." while Note 8 — Subsequent events lists "Participants are allowed to make Roth contributions" under a restated adoption agreement effective January 1, 2026, after the plan year reported. Asked that section ALONE the shipped extractor returns roth=true, so the Roth flag is DOUBLY CAUSED and a negation veto alone would leave it wrong. WITHDRAWN BY v207 (2026-11-21): the store now holds the flag FALSE with the denial quote retained as the evidence for the withdrawal, mirrored 13a445fb. The pin's role flips to must-stay-withdrawn: this arm reappearing means a later change undid v207.
cases.quote: The Plan does not allow for Roth or after-tax contributions.

cases.verified: 2026-11-20, filing read at line 1038: "Except for highly compensated participants, participants are allowed to make contributions to the Plan in any combination of before-tax, after-tax and/or Roth contributions." Both arms are correct, and the sentence carries the words "allowed to make" — the exact token an over-wide negation veto keyed on allow/permit would destroy. It is the largest correct yes in the population.
cases.quote: Except for highly compensated participants, participants are allowed to make contributions to the Plan in any combination of before-tax, after-tax and/or Roth contributions.

cases.verified: 2026-11-22, filing read: Roth appears exactly THREE times and all three are the SS604 catch-up mandate ("Effective January 1, 2026, the Plan implemented the Roth catch-up contribution requirements under the Internal Revenue Code"), while the plan's own contributions note says over-50 catch-up contributions are PRETAX. 30,463 readers; the largest member of the 330-plan class. CATCHUP_MANDATE was already in the v206 arm and unreachable, because that arm is gated on !out.roth and this sentence had won the arm above it.

2026-11-22, filing read: the ONLY after-tax sentence is "On January 1, 2026, the Company amended the Plan to allow after-tax employee contributions." against a plan year ending 2025-12. 3,516 readers. Its own roth flag rests on a different sentence and must be KEPT, which is why the fixture declares one arm and not two.

2026-11-22, filing read: "In May 2026, the Plan was amended to allow for after-tax contributions." against a plan year ending 2025-12, and no other after-tax sentence. 2,666 readers. The amendment date is carried by a BARE month-and-year, which is why datesIn admits that shape.

2026-11-22, filing read: "In September 2026, the Plan was amended to (i) permit participants to make voluntary after-tax contributions to the Plan..." against a plan year ending 2025-12. 226 readers. Roth is separately stated ("Roth elective deferrals (after-tax) when contributed to the Plan") and is KEPT.

2026-11-22, filing READ and the answer is the OPPOSITE of the one proposed for it. Asphalt Materials (3,100) was briefed as a must-withdraw. Its filing mentions Roth four times: a 2026 amendment-list item, the SS603 catch-up mandate, and TWICE "The participants salary redirection contributions and Roth contributions will be suspended for the six-month period following the distribution" — a plan provision that cannot exist unless Roth contributions do. v208 therefore KEEPS the flag and MOVES the quote off the amendment item onto the provision. accuracy-log 2026-11-22 (04:xxZ) lists it among the veto's GENUINE errors, i.e. a yes a terminal veto would wrongly destroy; it is the re-search's reason for existing, not its target.

2026-11-22, filing READ, and it is why `restrictsExisting` exists. Arcadium Lithium (482) was briefed as a must-withdraw. Its after-tax quote is "Effective March 31, 2026, the Plan was frozen and contributions under the Plan are temporarily suspended, including after-tax contributions" — a future-dated SUSPENSION presupposes the feature — and the SAME filing states it independently: "Participants may designate contributions as Roth contributions or as other after-tax contributions." That second sentence is refused by lib-4i's `rothModifies` guard on the words "or as other", so the re-search alone could not recover it and the first version of v208 withdrew a TRUE flag from 482 readers.

2026-11-22: "Effective January 1 2026, the Plan documents has been amended to increase the contribution limit of after-tax contributions from 10% to 20% of compensation." A DEGREE change presupposes the feature — after-tax plainly existed at 10% in the year reported — so the date test must not withdraw it. 2,485 readers.

2026-11-22: after-tax quote "X Change the limit for voluntary after tax contributions to 12%" is a degree change and must be kept; its roth quote ("Roth contributions and voluntary (after-tax) contributions are also permitted under the Plan") carries no date at all and is the control that the date test is silent where there is no date. 878 readers.

2026-11-22: "Additionally, effective January 1, 2026, the Company increased the after-tax contribution maximum from $10,000 to $29,500 for the 2026 Plan year." This is the member that caught the grant veto being spelled `add\\w*`, which matches "Additionally" — a character class written for a concept, met on a stem. 310 readers. NOTE: the briefed ack for Stonepeak was Stonepeak Ceramics; the plan that carries this sentence is Stonepeak Partners LP.
